text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CONSUMER WANTS SHOPS TO BE OPEN ON SUNDAYS

A Gallup poll shows that three of each five residents in Sao Paulo city are not only in favor of having shops open on Sundays but also would go shopping on that day. Sixteen percent of those polled said they could buy more on Sundays.
-- BRAZIL ATTEMPTS TO IMPROVE RATING

U.S. rating agency Moody's Investor Services is in Brazil gathering information about the country's public and foreign accounts and the banking system after the Real stabilization Plan. Central Bank Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco spent part of his day on Thursday "selling" the good image of the Real Plan to Moody's officials on expectations of an upgrade of the country's rating.
-- BRAZIL CRITICIZES WORLD BANK AT THE WTO

Brazil criticized the World Bank's action during a meeting of the World Trade Organization (WTO) in Geneva. Complaints involved a study by World Bank's economist Alexander Yeats who said the Mercosur trade agreement has helped inefficient industries.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- BROKEN WIRE MAY HAVE CAUSED PLANE CRASH
An electronic malfunction due to a broken wire that activated an engine thrust reverser may have caused last week's downing of a TAM's Fokker-100 aircraft that killed 98 people in Sao Paulo.
-- HOSPITAL IN NITEROI TO TRANSFER BABIES TODAY
A hospital in Niteroi, Rio de Janeiro state, will begin transferring babies to other hospitals in the region after eleven babies died in the past 15 days probably due to a bacterial infection.
-- SINGLE TAX MAY BECOME COMPULSORY

A federal government decree that created a single tax for small companies may be altered to oblige Brazilian states to accept the tax. According to the decree, small companies will be allowed to pay a single tax of between 5.0 percent and 7.5 percent, depending on the firm's revenues.
O GLOBO
-- SOCIAL SECURITY WILL DELAY 13TH SALARY TO PENSIONERS
The Social Security Ministry will delay the payment of the 13th salary to pensioners and retired workers. Without funds, the ministry will borrow money from private banks to pay the bonus.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
